sub_areas.name: Old Town
sub_areas.note: The primary town site at the mouth of the Niagara River (Wikipedia: 'the primary town site of Niagara-on-the-Lake (the Old Town)'). Its historic centre is the Town's only Part V Heritage Conservation District, the Queen-Picton Heritage Conservation District, approved 1986; exterior alterations there need Council consent and a heritage permit in addition to any building permit (Town heritage page). OGS point queries at the reference coordinate (43.25, -79.07) and at Queen Street (43.2554, -79.0717) return unit 8a fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay; bedrock at the reference coordinate is Queenston Formation, and the Queen Street point falls outside the MRD 219 bedrock polygons (no feature returned).

sub_areas.name: Virgil
sub_areas.note: 'Just southwest of the Old Town', home of the sports park and a large Mennonite community (Wikipedia); Town Hall is at 1593 Four Mile Creek Road, Virgil (Building Services brochure). OGS point query at the OSM village node (43.2214, -79.1229) returns unit 5d clay-to-silt till over Queenston Formation. A second point at 43.20, -79.09 (Niagara Stone Road / Concession 2 area, task-chosen) also returns 5d over Queenston.

sub_areas.name: St. Davids
sub_areas.note: Village in the southern part of the municipality below the Niagara Escarpment (Wikipedia lists it among the Town's settlements; St. Davids Public School 'serves ... the southern part of the municipality'). OGS point query at the OSM village node (43.1584, -79.1023) returns unit 8a fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay over Queenston Formation. No article-level coordinate exists on Wikipedia; the escarpment-buried-gorge geology mentioned in the task hints was not verified.

sub_areas.name: Queenston
sub_areas.note: Village on the Niagara River at Queenston Heights on the Niagara Escarpment, 'at the point where the Niagara River began eroding the Niagara Escarpment'; site of the former Queenston Quarry (Wikipedia). The Queenston Formation is named for it (Wikipedia: named for Queenston, Ontario, by J. F. Caley, 1940). OGS point queries at the Wikipedia/OSM coordinate (43.1642, -79.0546) and at 43.163, -79.053 return unit 8a silt and clay over Queenston Formation red shale.

sub_areas.name: Glendale
sub_areas.note: 'Near the junction of the Queen Elizabeth Way, Highway 405, and Highway 55, and adjacent to the Welland Canal'; home of Niagara College's Niagara-on-the-Lake campus and a large outlet mall (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the college campus (43.1526, -79.1650) returns unit 8a silt and clay over Queenston Formation. A task-chosen point 2 km south-east at 43.132, -79.155, on the escarpment brow, returns unit 8a over Lockport Formation dolostone, so bedrock type changes within the Glendale area.

sub_areas.name: Lakeshore / Niagara Parkway band north of Old Town
sub_areas.note: Task-chosen point at 43.24, -79.08 (between the Old Town and the Niagara River near the Parkway) returns OGS unit 9 coarse-textured glaciolacustrine sand and gravel over Queenston Formation. This is the only sand-and-gravel return in the town; the 'Niagara River delta sands' name in the task hints is not carried in the OGS layer and was not verified.

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 8a - Fine-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Silt and clay, minor sand and gravel; massive to well laminated (OGS layer attributes). Regionally these are the glacial Lake Iroquois plain sediments, but that lake name is not carried in the OGS attributes and was not verified here.
surficial.where: The dominant unit: query points at the reference coordinate (43.25, -79.07), Old Town Queen Street (43.2554, -79.0717), St. Davids (43.1584, -79.1023), Queenston (43.1642, -79.0546 and 43.163, -79.053), Glendale / Niagara College (43.1526, -79.1650) and the escarpment brow south-east of Glendale (43.132, -79.155) all return 8a.

surficial.description: Clay to silt-textured till (derived from glaciolacustrine deposits or shale) (OGS layer attributes).
surficial.where: The Virgil upland in the centre of the municipality: query points at the Virgil village node (43.2214, -79.1229) and at 43.20, -79.09 return 5d.

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 9 - Coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Sand, gravel, minor silt and clay (OGS layer attributes).
surficial.where: A narrow band between the Old Town and the Niagara River: query point 43.24, -79.08 returns unit 9. No other query point returned sand or gravel.

bedrock.formation: Queenston Formation (Upper Ordovician) under the whole lake plain; Lockport Formation (Silurian) on the Niagara Escarpment brow in the south-west corner of the municipality (OGS MRD219).
bedrock.description: Queenston: red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds (primary lithology shale). Returned at the reference coordinate, Virgil (both points), St. Davids, Queenston (both points), Glendale / Niagara College and the lakeshore band. Lockport: thick-bedded blue-grey crinoidal limestone to dolostone (Gasport Member), light brown dolostone (Goat Island Member), argillaceous dolostone and shale (Vinemount shale beds) and dark brown bituminous dolostone (Eramosa Member); returned only at 43.132, -79.155 on the escarpment brow south-east of Glendale. The Queenston Formation's type area is Queenston itself (Wikipedia: named for Queenston, Ontario).
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). No query point returned OGS unit 3 (bedrock at or near surface); every point sits on glaciolacustrine silt and clay, till or sand of unstated thickness. Queenston red shale is exposed in the Niagara Escarpment face and gorge at Queenston (Wikipedia), but no on-site depth figure was found.

implications_for_piles: The Town of Niagara-on-the-Lake publishes no deck sample drawing, footing depth or helical-pile note online: the Building Services page says only that accurate drawings and a site plan are required, that drawings must be by the owner or a BCIN-qualified designer, and that 'engineered drawings' may be required depending on construction. Pile depth, torque and capacity therefore rest on the installer's engineer, not on a municipal figure.

OGS maps fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8a) under the Old Town, St. Davids, Queenston and Glendale, and clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) under Virgil; these are the two soil textures a site design must address, and the OGS attributes give no bearing or shrink-swell values.

A sand-and-gravel band (unit 9) is mapped between the Old Town and the Niagara River (query point 43.24, -79.08); soil texture can change within a few hundred metres of the Old Town, so a reading from one street is not transferable to the next.

Bedrock is Queenston red shale across the lake plain and Lockport dolostone on the escarpment brow south-east of Glendale; the OGS returns give no depth, so refusal-on-rock is a site condition to confirm, not a mapped one.

Old Town properties inside the Queen-Picton Heritage Conservation District (Part V, approved 1986) and individually designated Part IV properties need a heritage permit for exterior alterations in addition to the building permit; the Town's heritage page says any alterations to Part V properties or the exterior of structures on them require the consent of Council and a heritage permit.

permits.authority: Town of Niagara-on-the-Lake Building Services (the page also uses 'Building Department' and 'Building Division', email building.division@notl.com; the heritage page refers to the 'Planning, Building and Development Services Department'). Niagara Region is the upper tier and is listed by the Town only as a separate contact agency.
permits.deck_permit_required_when: Building Services page: 'Permits are required for most construction activities, including buildings greater than 108 square feet, inground and above-ground swimming pools, and decks greater than 24" above grade.' The same page's FAQ lists 'uncovered decks that are 2 feet or greater above finished grade' among works needing a permit, and 'any other structure that is 108 square feet (10 square metres) or greater'. No covered-deck threshold is stated, but the fee schedule carries a separate 'Covered deck/porch' line.
permits.footing_depth_requirement: Not published. The Town posts no deck guide or sample drawings online; the Building Services page requires drawings to scale by the owner or a BCIN-qualified designer, a site plan (a Sample Site Plan PDF is linked) and, depending on the construction, 'engineered drawings'. Nothing retrieved mentions helical piles, CCMC or BMEC.
inspections: Not itemised online: the Town states 'Inspection stages are outlined when a permit is issued' and that the owner or contractor must request each inspection before the next stage of construction.
Re-inspection fee due to improper work, not ready or similar: $145.00 flat (2026 fee schedule); additional inspection request not identified in regulation: $191.00.
Building Inspector contact: (905) 468-3266 ext. 259, to be called early in planning to determine whether other approvals are needed.
permits.fee_note: 2026 Building User Fees & Service Charges: Residential uncovered deck less than 300 sq ft $230.00 each; uncovered deck greater than 300 sq ft $263.00 each; covered deck/porch $0.61 per sq ft; minimum permit fee $230.00; work started before a permit is issued doubles the applicable fee. The 2026 Building Services brochure still prints the January 1, 2024 figures ($150 / $172), which are superseded. Fees are payable when applying.
permits.timeline_note: No day-count is published. The page describes the sequence: zoning review, plans examination against the Ontario Building Code, review by a Building Inspector, then the Chief Building Official signs and issues the permit; incomplete drawings are not accepted and may delay issuance. Old Town properties in the Queen-Picton Heritage Conservation District (Part V) or individually designated (Part IV) also need Council consent and a heritage permit for exterior alterations.
permits.portal_note: Building permit applications are accepted only online through Cloudpermit; the Town links a 'Getting Started with Cloudpermit' PDF (April 2023) and a Cloudpermit support site. Public entry point: https://www.notl.com/building-services.

code.note: Null because the Town of Niagara-on-the-Lake publishes no deck guide or sample drawing that prints a footing depth; the only municipal text retrieved requires scaled drawings, a site plan and, where applicable, engineered drawings. The Ontario Building Code clause text was not retrieved (ontario.ca/laws renders O. Reg. 332/12 as a JavaScript shell and the 2024 Building Code Compendium is sold through Publications Ontario). Neighbouring Halton municipalities' drawings (Oakville, Milton) print 4'-0", but those documents do not govern Niagara-on-the-Lake and are not cited here. Do not cite a clause number.
